messages:
carol-support: Customer on hosted inference (eu-west) reporting spikes of 502/504 from their API clients since ~10:28 UTC. They see long tails of failed streams and a few 524s from Fastly. sample trace ids: trace=trc_9a8b, trc_9a9c. Can infra take a quick look?
ben-infra: seeing surge in handshake timeouts and connection resets on gateway. Error pattern lines up with cert push at 10:27:58. Logs: `tls_handshake: timeout after 10s, remote_ip=52.30.10.5` :eyes:
diana-sre: checked NAT/egress metrics for eu-west. conntrack entries jumped from 120k -> 510k around 10:28. SNAT ports exhausted on a subset of hosts (port range 32768-60999) leading to ephemeral-port starvation -> half-open sockets and handshake stalls.
alice-support: customer says they have many short-lived parallel streams (websocket-ish reconnects) during a rollout. They noted errors started immediately after the nightly cert rotation.
carlos-net: deploy-bot shows cert job `certpush-2026-03-17-eu` finished at 10:27:58; ACME issuer rotated intermediates and we updated LB certs. However DNS TTL for an internal egress VIP was still 300s and some nodes kept resolving an old egress NAT node IP. Mixed pathing + SNAT exhaustion = inconsistent flows and TCP resets.
ben-infra: reproducer snippet from a repro host: `for i in {1..2000}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate & done` -> immediate 502s once ephemeral ports hit limit.
diana-sre: quick mitigation options: 1) expand ephemeral port range + reduce TIME_WAIT (sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range & net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout) 2) add an additional SNAT pool / NAT gateway to offload 3) rollback cert push if we think cert change triggered client reconnect storm.
sam-engineer: applied temporary ip_local_port_range bump on 3 hosts in eu-west-2: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='10240 65535'` and reduced `tcp_tw_reuse=1`. Conntrack dropped and handshake success rate improved to ~98% for those hosts.
carol-support: conveyed the mitigation to the customer; they confirm degraded success but still occasional 502s from other hosts. Customer asks root cause and long-term fix. :thinking_face:
carlos-net: long-term: we need autoscaling for our SNAT gateways and standardize lower DNS TTLs around any rollout that touches egress IPs. Also ensure cert rotation jobs sequence LB update then drain then publish to avoid simultaneous client reconnects.
ben-infra: created infra ticket INF-3245 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3245) to: autoprov SNAT capacity in eu regions, add pre-rotation egress-warmup, and tighten DNS TTLs for internal VIPs. Assigned to eng-infra.
deploy-bot: certpush-2026-03-17-eu: job succeeded; changed cert chain from A->B. Rollout metadata: ratio=100%, started=10:27:30, finished=10:27:58.
diana-sre: also found a DNS TTL mismatch — some edge nodes cached old egress IP for ~4m due to intermediate resolver not honoring negative cache on DNS change. Add resolvers backpressure check.
alice-support: customer wants repro steps so they can verify once we fix. Suggested steps: 1) run a parallel curl loop (see ben's snippet) 2) observe increased SYN_SENT / TIME_WAIT on egress box 3) watch for 502/524 on client.
sam-engineer: logging note for postmortem: capture `ss -s`, `conntrack -L | wc -l`, and `journalctl -u redwood-egress` at time of spike. Also save TLS backend logs showing `handshake=timeout` and `tcp_retransmits`.
carol-support: summarizing for customer: probable root cause = simultaneous client reconnect storm (triggered by cert rotation) + egress SNAT ephemeral port exhaustion exacerbated by inconsistent DNS/TLS routing during rollout. Short-term fix applied (ephemeral port bump + SNAT offload), long-term actions in INF-3245. Customer asked for SLA credit evaluation — forwarded to billing.
ben-infra: next steps for us: 1) validate SNAT autoscaling prototype in staging 2) add pre-rotation warmup / drain step to cert push 3) lower TTLs for egress VIPs and monitor resolver cache behaviors. I'll post a short postmortem in #postmortems when INF-3245 updates land. :memo:
carol-support: thanks everyone. I'll keep the customer updated and close the loop once INF-3245 has milestones. :thumbsup:
